Looking into the history of this code block it seems that it was introduced to fix an issue where we would not auto scroll the text field to a visible position when first tapping on it https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/75604. At the time this change landed `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState` did not exist and was not called fom `formatAndSetValue`.

In it's current state `formatAndSetValue` does call `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState`. On iOS this handles both drags and long presses, while on Android only drags. 

The reason this bug is only presenting itself on Android and not iOS, is that when updating its selection, iOS always updates the moving edge to be the extent. Since `_scheduleShowCaretOnScreen` attempts to show the caret on screen (the extent of the selection), and we are always moving he extent, we always bring the moving edge into view as expected. On Android, if we move the start edge that is always going to move the `baseOffset` of the selection, similarly moving the end edge is always going to move the `extentOffset`. So when selecting backwards from the bottom of some long text, moving the start edge, `_scheduleShowCaretOnScreen` will always try to reveal the `extentOffset` even though we are moving the `baseOffset` and want to keep it in view.

A side note is that `TextFieldState._handleSelectionChanged` also calls `bringIntoView` when the selection changes because of a long press. Which would be called in `_handleSelectionChanged` before `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState` is called. These however do not conflict since on Android `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState` only handles drags and not long presses. On iOS we may be potentially calling `bringIntoView` twice. This should probably be addressed in a seperate PR.

This list ends on *"A drag n drop interface to upload files"* — the exact kind of controller that breaks when combined with the Turbo Streams section above, and the guide never covers that seam. A controller whose root element survives a Turbo Stream replacement never gets `connect()` called again, so per-element setup done there applies only to the elements present on page load. We shipped this twice: dead drop targets, and charts that stopped re-rendering after a morph. Silent no-ops both times, with green suites.

The example below deliberately uses bullet two from this same list, so it needs no third-party library.

````suggestion
* A _drag n drop_ interface to upload files.

### Controllers and Turbo

Turbo Streams and morphing replace elements in place. When a controller's root element
survives such a replacement, Stimulus does not call `connect()` again — so per-element setup
performed there applies only to the elements present the first time. Use the per-target
lifecycle callbacks instead; Stimulus calls them for every target as it enters or leaves the
DOM, including targets delivered by a Turbo Stream:

```js
export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = ["autogrow"]

  #observers = new Map()

  autogrowTargetConnected(textarea) {
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(() => {
      textarea.style.height = `${textarea.scrollHeight}px`
    })

    observer.observe(textarea)
    this.#observers.set(textarea, observer)
  }

  autogrowTargetDisconnected(textarea) {
    this.#observers.get(textarea)?.disconnect()
    this.#observers.delete(textarea)
  }
}
```

Prefer `data-action` for ordinary event handling — morphing and Turbo Streams preserve it.
The lifecycle callbacks are for what `data-action` cannot express: creating an object for an
element, observing it, or wiring a listener that must be removed again.
````
